column2: Face analysis takes a long time: can I pause or stop it?
column3: Yes. The analysis runs separately, without freezing the app: you can keep clicking meanwhile. The bar shows how many photos are done, the time per photo and the estimated time remaining. “⏸ Pause” stops after the current photo, “▶ Resume” starts again; “■ Stop” cuts straight away. Progress is kept: even after closing the window, “▶ Resume” starts again where you stopped. An unreadable photo, or one that takes much longer than the others (at least a minute and a half), is skipped and noted, without blocking the others; “↻ Retry the skipped photos” does them again.

column2: DNA: how do I group my matches and guess where to place a cousin?
column3: DNA tab → “🔗 Automatic groups”: matches that match each other (shared matches noted or imported, overlapping segments) form clusters, shown in a coloured matrix; each cluster gets its frequent names and places, its side, and the common ancestral couple (certain if a match is already linked to a record, probable from the names in the tree). One click sorts them into groups. “📍 Place a cousin”: for a match (or cM typed by hand), the possible relationships (Shared cM Project) then the couples in your tree they probably descend from, with a percentage and the clues (side, names, places, cluster, age); “Keep” notes it in the match. The test must be linked to the record of the tested person. It is a lead, never a proof.

column2: On which sites should I look for an ancestor? (🌍 Where to look?)
column3: On the record, the “🌍 Where to look?” block (or ⋯ → “🌍 Where to look?”, or Research → Type of research → “🌍 Where to look?”) suggests the sites to consult, the most useful first, according to their places (country, department), their period, their life (soldier → Mémoire des hommes and military registers, sailor → maritime register, emigrant → Ellis Island, Castle Garden, notary or inheritance → Minutier central…) and what is missing (unknown birth → the registers of their commune…). Each line says why; “↗ Search” opens the site in your browser with their name already filled in. “✓ Already searched” notes the result (Found, Nothing found, To review) in the Research log; ⋯ → “＋ Make it a lead” adds it to their investigation. “Free only” hides paid sites (the same setting as in Online archives). Any new site added to “Search the Internet” is taken into account automatically.

column2: What is a “brick wall” and how do I work on it?
column3: An ancestor where you are stuck: one or both of their parents are unknown. Research → Type of research → “🧩 Brick walls” lists them automatically, from the nearest generation to the most distant (Sosa), along with those you marked by hand (record → ⋯ → “🧱 I’m stuck here”, or “＋ Add a wall…”). “Open” shows what has already been searched (Log, letters, leads), the sites to try (🌍 Where to look?), the clues in your database (same name, born 20 to 50 years earlier; godparents and witnesses; household in a census; DNA) and a note. The status (To search, In progress, Solved, Abandoned) changes in one click, with “↶ Undo”; when the parents arrive in the database, the wall turns “Solved” by itself, with a well done. The “🧩 Brick walls” widget shows them on the dashboard, and “🗓 My research week” suggests one per week.

column2: How do I prove that an ancestor really is the son (or daughter) of someone? (⚖️ Proof file)
column3: Open a proof file: on the record, ⋯ → “⚖️ Proof file…” (choose the question: a parent, a couple, a date, a place, “same person as…”), or click the 🛡 badge next to a parent, or right-click on a box or a line of a tree in Charts. In the file: the question, the clues 👍 for and 👎 against (a text, the source or citation chosen in the picker, the kind of clue: direct, indirect or negative, the quality of the source: original, derivative or authored), the searches done (linked to the Research log), the conflicts between sources and how you resolve them, your conclusion and your level of certainty (proved, probable, possible, disproved, to check). Everything is saved by itself; a removed line comes back with “↶ Undo”. 🖨 Print and “📝 In the word processor” turn it into a document. All the files: Lists → Research and organisation → “⚖️ Proof files”.

column2: What is the “proof standard” the proof file talks about?
column3: The method of professional genealogists, in 5 steps: search widely (and note what you did not find), cite the source of each clue, weigh each clue (a record written on the day itself is worth more than a memory), explain the conflicts, write your conclusion. The proof file follows these 5 steps; “💡 How to reason?” recalls them in the window.

column2: What does the small 🛡 badge (Proved, Probable, Assumed, No source) next to the parents mean?
column3: It is the strength of the parent-child link, calculated by the app without changing anything in your database. In order: the proof file for this link if it has a conclusion; otherwise your choice by hand; otherwise the sources. Proved: a birth, baptism or marriage record of the child is cited and it names the parent (same source on the parent’s record, or their name written in the citation). Probable: a source names the parent elsewhere, or the birth record is cited without showing that it names this parent, or the citation is marked “secondary source”. Assumed: sources about the child, but none about this link (or marked unreliable, or a “doubtful” date). No source: nothing cited. Click the badge to see why, open the file or choose the level by hand (↶ Undo).

column2: How do I see the weak links in my tree? (🛡 Strength view, Weak branches)
column3: In Charts, on the ancestor tree, the descendant tree or the hourglass, switch on “🛡 Strength view”: each line takes the colour and thickness of its level (legend at the top; thick green = proved, blue = probable, yellow dashes = assumed, grey dots = no source, red = disproved). Lists → Research and organisation → “🛡 Weak branches” lists your Sosa ancestors whose link is assumed, without a source or disproved, from the nearest to the most distant, with “⚖️ File” and “🌍 Where to look?”. Also: the “🛡 Weak branches” widget and, each week, a “🛡 Link to strengthen” in “My research week”.

column2: Where can I see everything I have already searched, so as not to search the same place twice?
column3: Research → Type of research → “🗓 Research log” (the same log is in Lists → Archives and sources). Everything that has been searched, from the most recent to the oldest: record indexes, shelfmarks from archive visits done, investigation leads, communes of search sweeps, requests (records to order). Each line says where (service, shelfmark, commune, years), when, and the result (Found, Nothing found, Partly). The top bar searches for a shelfmark, a commune or a name, and filters by kind, result, person, archive service or commune; “List | Cards”, sort, “⤓ Export as CSV”. A click opens the item in its tool.

column2: How do I note the result of a record index and who I did it for?
column3: Research → Archive record index → ✎ Edit (or ＋ Add a record index). “Result”: Found (green badge), Nothing found (grey) or Partly (yellow), in addition to the state and the free text. “People searched for”: choose the records of the people for whom you opened this register (several possible) — they stay separate from the people noted in it. The record index then appears in the “🔍 Already searched” block of their record.

column2: What does “⚠️ Already in your tracking” mean when I type a shelfmark?
column3: While you fill in a record index, a request (records to order) or an archive visit shelfmark, the app checks whether you have already searched in the same place: the same shelfmark (in the same service), or the same archive service + the same commune + the same type of record over overlapping years. If so, the message says what, with the result and the date (“Nothing found, on 12 March 2025”) and “↗ Open”. You can still save.

column2: After a visit to the archives, how do I note what I found?
column3: Lists → Archive visit planner → on the mission sheet, “✓ Done on…”: give the day of the visit. The sheet moves to the “✓ Visits done” tab (the past stays readable). For each shelfmark, choose the result (Found, Nothing found, Partly, Not consulted); “Edit” adds a note (“Record no. 12, image 34”). “＋ Create the record index” creates the shelfmark’s record index and links it (or links an existing record index with the picker in “Edit”). Each shelfmark goes into the Research log.

column2: How do I sort my documents by archive service (departmental archives, municipal archives, notaries…)?
column3: Lists → Archives and sources → “🏛 Archive services” → “＋ New service” (you can start from a department’s Departmental Archives: name, acronym and website fill in). On the service’s record: address, opening hours, website, series (“3 E — Notaries”), and “✓ Already consulted there”: all your record indexes, visits done and requests made at this service, sorted by series. In a source’s window and in a media item’s window, “🏛 Archive service” is chosen with the picker, with the series and the shelfmark. If you wrote a service by hand in your research (“AD 19”), the list offers to create its record; its other names (“AD Corrèze”…) are noted on the record.

column2: How do I get a ready-made citation of a source, in Evidence Explained or Chicago style or for a forum?
column3: On the record, next to each source (and each source of an event), “❝”: the same source written in four styles — classic French, Evidence Explained, Chicago, Geneanet / forum —, as a note and as a bibliography entry, each with “📋 Copy”. “⭐ My style” puts it first everywhere. “❝” at the top of the “Sources & citations” block gives all the record’s citations in one style: “📋 Copy all”, “⤓ Export as text”, “🖨 Print”. In a page layout, Text → “📚 Cite a source” has a “Style” menu (the note and the bibliography are written in that style); the research report (Settings → Exports) ends with the bibliography in your style.

column2: How do I compare two hypotheses (“born in Naves or in Tulle?”) and update the record?
column3: On the record, the “⚖️ Hypotheses” block → “＋ New hypothesis”: the question, the event concerned and the kind (Place, Date…). Then “⚖️ Compare”: one column per answer (the record’s value is already there; “＋ Another answer” adds a place, a date or a text). In each column, “👍 For” and “👎 Against”: add a source, a media item or a record index with the picker (or write the evidence), and give it a weight (weak, medium, strong). The column with the highest total (for − against) is “Leading”. “✓ Keep …” changes the place or the date of the event on the record and confirms the hypothesis; “↶ Undo” puts everything back as before. All hypotheses: Settings → Hypotheses.

column2: On a person’s record, where can I see what has already been searched for them?
column3: The “🔍 Already searched” block: the record indexes in which they are searched for or noted, the shelfmarks of visits done that concern them, the leads of their investigations, their search sweeps and the related requests — where, when, the shelfmark and the result, with “↗ Open”. “🗓 Log” opens the whole log filtered on them. The block can be arranged, set and hidden like the others (Settings → Appearance → record blocks).
